contract: Retain initial authored-source and projection validation before allocation.
Reauthenticate the existing plan after obtaining the materialization lock and before cache lookup/reuse; reject source movement while waiting.
Reauthenticate the existing plan after setup and before dependency installation; reject changed pyproject, gate registry or projection through existing typed errors and owned temporary cleanup.
Native pip consumes only the already derived closed immutable requirements tuple in every supported source mode. A later projection path read must not introduce unbound bytes after validation.
Metadata still requires a declared valid projection for materialization; authenticated source identity is not an executable projection.
Preserve normal CLI grammar, exact source-based identity, compatible dependency semantics and existing legacy/governed behavior. No alternate resolver, evaluator, receipt or authority policy.
expected_tests: Source movement at materialization-lock acquisition rejects before cache lookup or native work.
Projection, pyproject and gate-registry mutations during controlled setup each reject before pip; owned incomplete setup is cleaned.
Mutation at the final native install boundary cannot change dependency arguments from the exact derived tuple.
All existing projected-metadata/legacy/governed planning/materialization/reuse controls remain in the consumer module; actual environment and installed-runtime qualification remain separate.
forbidden_surfaces: Original frozen two-case RED checkout or packet
Maintenance source and immutable release assets
Claims of executed exploit or verified fix before causal execution

source_observation.finding: Metadata pip_arguments reads a mutable requirements path after initial validation and setup; no source recheck exists after materialization lock or setup.

verification: Contract then tests then production. Existing 84-case scope is historical until new exact collection and execution. Full P32/P33 requirements and release remain open.
